title: Microsoft (MSFT) Stock: Dip as ChatGPT Outage Hits Paid Plans and Cloud Codex - Blockonomi
content: Microsoft (MSFT) shares fell $15.25, or 3.07%, to $480.88 by 11:47 a.m. EST on Wednesday, November 25. Microsoft-backed OpenAI reported a service disruption that affected several paid ChatGPT plans. The incident extended to ChatGPT Work and cloud Codex threads during the same morning. Microsoft shares slipped below $480 shortly after the opening bell and then briefly rebounded above $485. The rebound faded later in the morning, and the stock gave up most of its recovery. Microsoft shares remained below the previous session’s closing price of $496.13 throughout the rebound. OpenAI reported more errors during conversations across multiple ChatGPT subscriptions, according to status updates cited by Seeking Alpha. The affected plans included Plus and Pro, along with Business and Team. OpenAI also listed the Education plan among the subscriptions affected by the service disruption. The list covered individual subscriptions as well as plans for teams and institutions. Plus and Pro serve individual subscribers, while Business and Team serve groups that use ChatGPT in the workplace. The Education plan extends access to members of academic institutions. ChatGPT Work extends the service to professional tasks, and cloud Codex supports software development through remote coding sessions. Both tools use conversation threads to receive requests and return results to users within the same thread. OpenAI tracked the errors across these tools under the same incident. For ChatGPT users, the reported errors could interrupt a conversation at several points during a session. Users could encounter an error when starting a new chat or sending a message in an existing thread. A conversation could also fail to return a response. OpenAI posted its status updates as the disruption unfolded on Wednesday. The company first identified the issue and began work on a fix for the errors across the affected services. It later applied measures to reduce the errors and moved to monitor their effect. After applying those measures, OpenAI reported signs of recovery across ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and cloud Codex threads. It continued monitoring service performance and investigating the cause. The update gave no timetable for full recovery. OpenAI reported the earlier incident on November 23, two days before the latest disruption. The company cited intermittent errors in GPT-6 conversations on paid ChatGPT plans. Its official status history shows that OpenAI resolved the earlier disruption later that Monday. Wednesday’s notice covered a wider set of services than Monday’s GPT-6 incident. OpenAI reported progress on Wednesday, but its update stopped short of declaring the incident resolved. title: Microsoft (MSFT) Stock: Code Red Sets a One-Hour Clock for Global Fixes - Blockonomi
content:
Microsoft (MSFT) has launched a “Code Red” overhaul of how it prevents and handles major service failures. The move follows a 24-hour outage on November 12 and 13, according to internal memos reviewed by Reuters. JUST IN: Microsoft $MSFT declares "Code Red" after a 24-hour outage exposed major flaws in its systems. The outage hit Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other Microsoft 365 products. Microsoft blamed an undetected Windows scalability defect introduced in July. The company said the incident was not tied to cyber activity or AI agents. CEO Satya Nadella has publicly apologized for the disruption. Jason Henderson, president of M365 Core, called it the most customer-impacting incident in Exchange Online’s history. Never before had so many customers been without email for so long, he said. “Code Red means that this is the highest priority work for our team,” Henderson told staff on Friday. He will hold daily meetings with the Substrate leadership team, plus weekly reviews. Corporate vice president Amanda Silver said engineers worked through a “fog of war” as the outage unfolded. Her memo landed on Monday. Responders exchanged more than 11,000 messages across 11 Teams chats. That is a lot of typing for one outage. Diagnostic data sat in fragmented internal tracking systems. Silver said that made it hard to keep a cohesive picture of hypotheses and decisions. Charles Lamanna, executive vice president of Copilot, Agents and Platform, told a review the affected component had seen “roughly ten years’ worth of acceptable failures.” Silver’s memo included the remark. The outage also reached Microsoft Defender for Office 365, Defender XDR and Purview. At the peak, more than 130,000 Outlook complaints were recorded. Integrations used by OpenAI and Anthropic were also affected. The disruption reached governments in Australia, Japan and the United States, and it delayed trading firms and airline communications. Silver outlined five workstreams focused on load shedding, geographic traffic partitioning and faster recovery tools. Microsoft also plans to use AI agents to help engineers read system health data faster. The target is worldwide resolution within an hour during future incidents. Henderson said urgent patches to M365 Core services have taken too long to deploy. In one recent incident, an urgent production fix took five to six days to reach worldwide saturation. “Needless to say, we aren’t here yet,” he wrote. For the most urgent security issues, he wants detection to safe worldwide deployment in an hour. A company spokesperson said teams keep working around the clock on lessons learned. Earlier this month, outages also touched Apple, United Airlines, JPMorgan Chase and an FAA-linked ground stop. Jay Clayton, Director of National Intelligence, dismissed cyberattack concerns. content: Microsoft's MSFT accelerating AI infrastructure build-out is testing investor patience as capital spending weighs on free cash flow. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, capital expenditures, including $7.4 billion of finance leases, totaled $45.2 billion, with roughly three-fourths directed toward short-lived assets, primarily CPUs and GPUs. Cash paid for property and equipment was $39.4 billion compared with $19.4 billion a year ago, leaving free cash flow at $18.6 billion, even as operating cash flow rose 29% to $58 billion. Spending is fueling growth. Revenues climbed 19% to $92.3 billion, while operating income increased 21% to $45.9 billion. Microsoft Cloud revenues rose 30% to $63.9 billion, and Azure revenues surged 48% to $33.2 billion. Commercial remaining performance obligation jumped 73% to $677 billion, with roughly 30% expected to be recognized over the next 12 months, offering visibility into future returns. Microsoft also returned $10.2 billion to shareholders via dividends and share repurchases. However, the investment cycle is far from peaking. Microsoft expects second-quarter fiscal 2027 capital expenditures to exceed $50 billion and calendar-year spending of about $170 billion, with fiscal second-half spending accelerating, primarily on CPUs. Second-quarter revenues are projected at $96-$97.1 billion, with Azure growth of 49-50% in constant currency. However, operating expenses are expected to rise 9% and operating margin is likely to decline slightly year over year. Commercial bookings fell 12% in the first quarter. Customer demand continues to exceed available supply. Efficiency initiatives offer a partial offset. In November 2026, Microsoft made Cobalt 200 virtual machines generally available with up to 50% better performance than the prior generation and expanded its long-term agreement with Intel, securing multi-year Xeon supply. Management expects to remain free cash flow positive in fiscal 2027, but near-term cash conversion is likely to stay pressured, making the stock better suited for long-term investors. Alphabet GOOGL reported third-quarter capital expenditures of $51.4 billion, resulting in negative free cash flow of $9.1 billion. According to reports citing sources familiar with the matter, an internal memo reveals that U.S. tech giant Microsoft (MSFT.US) has launched a special initiative called "Code Red" to comprehensively improve its mechanisms for preventing and responding to major service outages. Previously, a 24-hour outage exposed weaknesses in its engineering systems and global IT crisis response capabilities. According to reports, the major outage on November 12–13 affected government agencies in countries including Australia, Japan, and the United States, delayed business operations at trading institutions, and disrupted airline communications, heightening concerns about the vulnerability of critical digital infrastructure. Microsoft stated that the incident was unrelated to cyberattacks or AI-powered hacking activities. This outage and the large-scale disruption represent the most severe incident in the history of Microsoft's cloud-based enterprise email and collaboration hosting service, Exchange Online, affecting the largest number of customers. Outlook, Teams, and Copilot were also impacted. Upon investigation, Microsoft found that after certain gateway failures, the redirected traffic triggered the same software defect on gateways in other regions, causing the outage to spread across regions. Microsoft plans to isolate traffic by region, prioritize critical services during overload, and use AI agents to accelerate fault diagnosis, aiming to restore global services within one hour in similar incidents in the future. This major Microsoft outage has added a measurable metric to the enterprise cloud competition: AI capabilities can win Microsoft more contracts, but whether customers are willing to further consolidate their email, collaboration, and AI workflows onto a single platform also depends on how widespread the disruption is and how quickly critical business operations can be restored. Microsoft has sounded the "red alert"—why did a gateway flaw escalate into nearly 24 hours of downtime? A single software defect affected Microsoft 365 gateways across multiple regions. After some gateways failed, traffic was rerouted to other regions; the receiving gateways experienced increased load, which in turn triggered the same defect, ultimately resulting in a region-wide cascading failure. As of the close on November 24 Eastern Time, Microsoft rose 0.74% to $496.13, while the Nasdaq Composite Index fell 1.5% on the same day. Microsoft's post-incident review revealed that the defect was located in Microsoft 365's network gateway. During peak business hours, some gateways were undergoing maintenance, and Teams traffic had already been switched to shared gateways. After the failure occurred, the traffic shift further increased the load on other gateways, which suffered from the same defect, causing the outage to spread across regions. In other words, after some gateways failed, the diverted traffic triggered the same software defect on other gateways, causing the outage to spread across regions. Jason Henderson, president of Microsoft 365's core business, said in a memo to employees on Friday that this is the most severe outage in Exchange Online's history affecting customers. He said that never before have so many customers been unable to access email for such a prolonged period. "A red alert means this is our team's highest-priority task," Henderson added. Amanda Silver, a Microsoft corporate vice president responsible for the core business of Microsoft 365 and the Work IQ platform for intelligent agent work scenarios, said in another memo on Monday that as the outage continued to unfold, engineers had to operate in "fog of war." Silver said that despite Microsoft mobilizing its top engineers, the emergency response team still exchanged over 11,000 messages across 11 Teams chats. Because diagnostic data was scattered across siloed internal tracking systems, the team struggled to maintain a unified view of the troubleshooting hypotheses and decisions made at the time. "Red Alert" is the highest-priority mobilization mechanism reserved for major crises. Silver outlined five tasks, with key focuses including proactively offloading some load, isolating traffic by geographic region, and establishing faster recovery mechanisms. The company also plans to deploy AI agents to help engineers analyze data reflecting system performance more quickly. Henderson said he will meet daily with the Substrate leadership team to track progress on post-incident actions and conduct weekly reviews. The team oversees the engineering division that supports the underlying services of Microsoft 365. A Microsoft spokesperson said the company will promptly resolve the issues that have arisen and do everything possible to prevent similar outages from happening again in the future. He added that he has launched an in-depth review of the broader organizational and structural issues that led to the failure. For the most critical security issues, we need to complete the entire process—from identifying the problem to deploying the patch worldwide—within one hour. Clearly, we haven't achieved that yet." Falcon Guardian, which specifically protects agents, surpassed $100 million in ARR after the quarter ended. CrowdStrike management explained on the earnings call that Falcon can detect agent activity on devices and in the cloud, while Zscaler, which the company plans to acquire for an enterprise value of approximately $43.9 billion, can fill gaps in network and zero-trust access. On November 23, CrowdStrike closed down 8.92% on a day it reported strong financial results. title: Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT) Stock Price Sits 11% Below Record Highs Despite Monday's Nvidia-Driven Tech Rally - Foreign Policy Journal
content: By David Prior | Nov 24, 2026 | Economy & Business, Featured, News & Analysis Despite a broad surge in technology shares on Monday, Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT) remains a notable distance from its peak valuation, leaving investors to weigh whether the rebound signals a genuine recovery. The stock climbed during Monday’s session as part of a wider relief rally across the technology sector, with Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) credited as a key catalyst driving renewed buying interest. Even with the gains, Microsoft shares still trade roughly 11% below their all-time high, a gap that underscores how far the stock has yet to travel to reclaim its former record levels. The tech sector has been searching for directional conviction, and Monday’s move offered at least a short-term answer, with heavyweights across the industry participating in the upswing. Nvidia’s influence over broader technology sentiment has become a recurring theme in recent months, with the chipmaker’s performance frequently setting the tone for peers across the sector. A single session of gains rarely resolves deeper questions about valuation or near-term momentum, and Microsoft’s 11% deficit to its record price keeps those questions firmly on the table. For long-term shareholders, the gap to all-time highs represents both a concern and a potential opportunity, depending on how the company’s fundamental outlook develops in coming quarters. The relief rally dynamic suggests that sentiment, rather than fresh fundamental catalysts, was the primary driver behind Monday’s advance in technology equities broadly. Microsoft’s trajectory will likely depend on whether the tech sector can sustain upward momentum beyond a single session, or whether profit-taking pulls shares back toward recent trading ranges. With the stock still meaningfully below its record, the central question facing investors heading into the final weeks of 2026 is whether Monday’s Nvidia-fueled bounce marks a turning point or simply a temporary pause in a broader consolidation. title: China Is “Only 12 Hours” Behind US AI Labs. ByteDance’s Reported Azure Deal Puts Microsoft in the Middle - TIKR.com
content: Podcaster Dwarkesh Patel posted on X last week that “China is only 12 hours, not 12 months, behind the frontier AI labs.” And Microsoft (MSFT) may be about to give one of China’s biggest tech companies a faster way to those labs’ models. ByteDance, the Chinese company behind TikTok, is in advanced talks to spend about $500 million more on Azure, mostly to use OpenAI’s models, The Information reported. ByteDance turned to Azure after Anthropic cut it off. OpenAI keeps most Chinese companies off its own platform, and it has reportedly raised concerns about Chinese firms distilling its models. But OpenAI can’t stop the deal. Microsoft keeps the rights to OpenAI’s models and products through 2032, and it reportedly doesn’t apply OpenAI’s China limits on Azure. Azure isn’t the only cloud in this position. Amazon (AMZN) added OpenAI’s GPT-6 models to Bedrock, AWS’s AI service, last quarter. Microsoft brought in $332 billion of revenue in fiscal 2026 (the year to June), and analysts expect about $396 billion this fiscal year: Even if ByteDance spent the whole $500 million in one year, it would be less than 0.2% of last year’s revenue. The money wouldn’t change Microsoft’s financial results. TIKR tracks 58 analysts on Microsoft. How many say “Buy”? More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Microsoft’s Analyst Ratings So why would Microsoft want the deal? Its capital spending rose from $23.9 billion in fiscal 2022 to $116 billion in fiscal 2026, nearly 5x: All that capacity has to be sold to someone. Free cash flow fell to $67.0 billion in fiscal 2026, and consensus has it at $32.0 billion this fiscal year. No wonder Microsoft’s cloud team would sign any big customer willing to pay. Washington has limited China’s access to the most advanced chips. But a Chinese lab that can use the newest US models in the cloud can train its own models on their answers, and Patel’s “12 hours” suggests how quickly that can happen. The White House is also reportedly discussing a proposal that would require US companies to publicly disclose when they use Chinese open-weight models, as Abacus.AI CEO Bindu Reddy pointed out on X. She doubts a rule like that would hold: “Open-weights can’t be stopped easily.” My read: open-weight models are hard to police, so regulators may go after the clouds that sell US models first. That would affect Amazon too, since Bedrock sells Chinese open-weight models alongside OpenAI’s. Microsoft’s stock already trades below its usual multiple, at 23x forward earnings against a three-year average of 30x: I think that discount has much more to do with the capex bill than with China, and a $500 million deal won’t move it. If I were running Azure, I’d pass on this deal. It would make Azure the way a Chinese tech giant reaches US frontier models just as Washington decides where to draw the line on distillation. The deal also puts Microsoft at odds with OpenAI, which made up about 45% of Microsoft’s commercial backlog as of December 2025. Of course, the deal may never close, and the disclosure proposal is only being discussed. Until either changes, the number that matters more for the stock is free cash flow against that $32.0 billion consensus, with the December-quarter report due in late January. Free cash flow over the past twelve months was $60.0 billion, down from $78.0 billion in the twelve months to September 2025. Capital spending, including finance leases, reached $45.2 billion in fiscal Q1 2027, mostly on short-lived assets such as CPUs and GPUs. Microsoft expects to spend more than $50 billion in fiscal Q2 2027. That rising bill is what worries a holder. The signed contracts are Microsoft’s case for that bill. Microsoft says it is building against a growing book of business, and the signed contracts are the clearest measure of that book. Cash is coming in faster too. Cash from operations rose 29% to $58 billion in fiscal Q1 2027, on strong cloud billings and collections. Still, free cash flow fell even as the contracts grew. Microsoft also said it will tap other sources of funding when it finds them attractive. In late October 2026, a source said Microsoft expected to raise $25 billion in a US bond sale. What Could Show Microsoft’s Contracts Falling Short? New signings are where a slowdown would show first. Commercial bookings fell 12% in fiscal Q1 2027. Management put that down to large Azure commitments signed a year earlier. It expects bookings to swing sharply from quarter to quarter as such deals land. Supply is the other risk. Some third-party GPU contracts have slipped to the second half of fiscal 2027, which runs from January to June 2027. Even so, Microsoft expects Azure revenue to grow 49% to 50% in fiscal Q2 2027, excluding currency moves. Management said on the call that it needs more efficiency gains from its own fleet to get there. Microsoft is expected to report in January 2027. That report will show how Azure growth compares with that forecast, and how much the signed contracts have grown from a year earlier. We read Microsoft’s signed contracts as a stronger signal than its flat share price, though that is only our way of judging it. content: Microsoft (MSFT) closed at $497.73 after a muted 24-hour move of 0.25%, leaving shares just below the $498.30 pivot and beneath short-term moving averages. The latest quarter showed revenue of $92.... Microsoft’s latest reported quarter was solid: revenue came in at $92.3 billion, up 19%, operating income rose 21% to $45.9 billion, and diluted EPS reached $4.92 on a GAAP basis, up 32%, according to Microsoft’s October 28, 2026 results release. Microsoft Cloud revenue hit $63.9 billion, growing 30%, which is the cleanest fundamental support in the package of evidence here. That strength has not translated into a clean price trend. MSFT last traded at $497.73, essentially flat over 24 hours, and remains under its 7-day, 20-day, 50-day, 12-day EMA, and 26-day EMA. The moving average stack is bearish, with MA7 below MA20 and MA50, which tells you the rebound attempt is still fighting trend pressure rather than leading it. The stock is sitting close to the middle of a short-term decision zone. The immediate resistance is $501.83, with stronger resistance at $505.93. On the downside, immediate support is $494.20 and stronger support is $490.67. Momentum is mixed but still soft. Daily RSI is 39.73, which is neutral but leaning weak, while the MACD histogram is flat at 0.0000 with MACD and signal both at -8.2469. That does not show a fresh bearish acceleration, but it also does not show an upside breakout in progress. The Stochastic readings, %K at 24.00 and %D at 19.20, keep the stock in an oversold-leaning area without confirming a durable turn. Bollinger positioning reinforces that message. MSFT is near the lower band at $485.90, with %B at 0.1751, which means price is pressing the lower part of its recent range rather than reclaiming the middle band at $519.68. ATR(14) of $15.97 says volatility remains meaningful, so any move through support or resistance can travel quickly once it starts. Wall Street targets remain above the spot price. Stockanalysis.com cites 58 analysts with a consensus rating of Strong Buy and an average target of $636.12, with a low target of $440 and a high of $870. Benzinga reported an average target of $621.23 from 29 analysts, with all 29 rating the stock Buy. Recent notes include RBC Capital maintaining Outperform with a $640 target on November 20, TD Cowen reiterating Buy with a $650 target on November 18, and Bernstein lifting its target to $722 on October 29. The important distinction is that these are longer-horizon target levels, not a short-term timing signal. The near-term tape is still controlled by price structure, and that structure is weaker than the analyst backdrop. On Binance perpetual futures, funding is neutral at 0.0000%, which means there is no obvious cost bias forcing one side of the market. Open interest is 35,416.52 contracts, with a daily open interest value of $20,041,291 and a 24-hour OI change of -1.79%, suggesting some de-risking rather than aggressive build-up. The long/short ratios lean short. Binance global accounts show 41.9% long versus 58.1% short, while top-trader accounts show 44.2% long versus 55.8% short. The 1-hour taker buy/sell ratio of 0.6873, based on buy volume of 348 versus sell volume of 506, points to aggressive selling pressure in the latest window. That does not guarantee downside follow-through, but it does argue against calling the tape comfortably constructive. For MSFT to improve its near-term setup, it needs to reclaim $501.83 and then $505.93 with better volume than the current 0.38x of the 5-day average. If that happens, the stock can start rebuilding back toward the 20-day average at $519.68. If it loses $494.20, the next level that matters is $490.67. A clean break below that zone would leave the lower Bollinger band at $485.90 as the next magnet, and would keep the burden of proof on buyers despite the strong fundamental print.
